tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.
tools.name: clock

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.
tools.name: sleep

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.
tools.name: collaboration

tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.
tools.name: followup_task

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.
tools.name: interrupt_agent

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.
tools.name: list_agents

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.
tools.name: send_message

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.
tools.name: spawn_agent

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.
tools.name: wait_agent

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.
tools.name: mcp__cua_repl

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

V15 acceptance: **1,031 backend tests passed**, one existing TestClient warning,
227.13 seconds. Ruff, 164-file formatting, dependency and whitespace checks passed
on the frozen 167-file source. Its strict live L1/L2/L3 runs all failed: unnecessary
L1 help and an approved concurrency above its scenario cap; insufficient cumulative
L2 review budget; L3 revision followed by review-capacity exhaustion. No current-source
live level is accepted, and neither complex run reached its mid-execution restart.
Phase 2 remains incomplete. See the [current acceptance record](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-v15.md)
and [verification v15](docs/audit/phase2/verification-v15.json). Earlier-round results
below are historical; all 53 finished driver records are preserved in snapshot-v7.

Continued acceptance: the unchanged v12 backend baseline was rerun with 955 tests
passing and the existing TestClient deprecation warning (236.32 seconds). V13 adds
an advisory review-capacity snapshot to the Worker's existing allowance message.
It measures verified settled evidence without generating a delivery, reserving
tokens or changing execution/review state. Running estimates exclude the future
delivery and are neither admission lower nor upper bounds; the complete real
review packet, original 65,536-byte cap, provenance and PASS binding still apply.
No new dependency or startup configuration is required. The prior v12 verification
and its documentation are preserved in `docs/audit/phase2/checkpoint-v12/`.

V14 addresses known model usage settling after a Worker pause or process restart.
Schema 12 stores new local model reservations with their call and assignment
identity. One matching settled Gateway attempt can reconcile only that reservation
once; response handling still requires the original execution fence. Unknown
outcomes retain their reservations, and historical calls without this binding are
not inferred or refunded. No new startup setting or dependency is required.

Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. An earlier strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. Later L2/L3 reruns also failed before review at packet/context and cumulative-budget limits. The [v5 full backend suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v5.xml) passed 820 tests with one warning in 219.96 seconds, before later v6 changes. The [v6 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v6.xml) retained 848 passed, one failed, one warning / 283.77 seconds; all three v6 live reruns failed. V7 corrects independent Worker/Gateway concurrency and extends bounded handoff/budget guidance. The [v7 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v7.xml) passed 849 tests / one warning / 216.87 seconds, while all three v7 live attempts failed. The [v8 full suite](docs/audit/phase2/frozen-tests-v8.xml) passed 886 tests / one warning / 283.46 seconds; all three v8 live attempts failed, despite real review/revision and Worker archiving in L1/L2. L1/L2 each retain an unresolved Router-notice attempt and no mid-execution Core restart occurred. The v9 full suite passed 895 tests / one warning / 237.83 seconds; both v9 L2/L3 live runs still failed before review at the unchanged raw-packet cap. Thirty-nine finished driver records are published without changing original outcomes. The v10 full suite passed 915 tests / one warning / 279.54 seconds, while all three v10 strict live attempts failed. L2 did demonstrate actual research PASS, a settled mid-execution Core restart with two-source Router archive/readback and preserved counters, followed by architect continuation; the successor later blocked on the original receipt-read bound. Forty-two driver records are now published. V11 passed 941 tests / one warning / 199.39 seconds. Its L1 strict run passed after two real review revisions; L2 advanced through research/analysis revisions, report creation and a preserved restart, then hit final Worker context admission. L3 was blocked by an overly conservative serial-capacity precheck rather than actual Gateway budget exhaustion. V12 frozen testing passed 955 / one warning / 251.43 seconds. Its strict L1 passed after real review revision; L2 retained another restart/readback and real successor artifact but lacked review budget, while revised L3 hit original capacity/budget limits. Fifty driver records are published, including two further failed L2/L3 samples on the same frozen source. The last L3 retained a real research PASS, mid-execution restart/readback and mathematical successor continuation, then failed review-budget admission. Nine recorded unresolved attempts across the historical set are a lower bound; six early records lack usage statistics, so true aggregate usage/cost remain unknown. The final evidence record preserves this partial state and open gates. Phase 2 remains incomplete. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical recall and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. General autonomous replanning, learned semantic retrieval, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain open. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

Python 3.11+ recommended.

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
pytest
python -m forge_api
```

The lock file is verified on Windows with Python 3.13; other platforms and Python versions have not been verified. The editable installation requires build tooling already available. API documentation endpoints are disabled.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.

### Approved Worker execution

`python_test` runs bounded pure Python function tests against a governed workspace
file using an isolated subprocess and an AST interpreter. Its approved parameters
are `path`, `function` and `suite.cases` (1–32 input/expected cases). It supports

"""Explicit Core sizing measures resources, never supplies a semantic plan."""

import copy
import json

from test_planner_capacity_v17 import handoff_graph
from test_router_intelligence_phase2 import ScriptedMock
from test_verified_capacity_v16 import generate, prepared

from forge_core.capacity_preflight import verified_input_inventory
from forge_core.domain import DomainError
from forge_core.graph_domain import CapacityGraphWire
from forge_core.providers import ProviderConfig, ProviderGateway
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService


class NativeFramingMock(ProviderGateway):
    """Mock output plus production native serializer; no network calls."""

    def __init__(self, graph):
        super().__init__(
            ProviderConfig(
                id="p",
                kind="openai_compatible",
                base_url="https://example.invalid/v1",
                credential_ref="FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_TEST",
                supports_tools=True,
                supports_json_schema=True,
            )
        )
        self.graph = graph
        self.requests = []

    async def generate(self, request):
        self.requests.append(request)
        return type("MockResponse", (), {"text": json.dumps(self.graph), "usage": {}})()


def measured_graph():
    graph = handoff_graph()
    graph["allocation_mode"] = "core_measured_serial"
    graph["serial_capacity_policy"] = None
    # Deliberately impossible guesses: only explicit Core mode may replace them.
    for node in graph["nodes"]:
        node["budget_tokens"] = 900000
    return graph


def prepared_chain(tmp_path):
    return prepared(
        tmp_path,
        content='Assess inputs/unicode.json. Task execution limits: {"max_total_tokens":360000,"max_nodes":2,"max_members":2}',
    )


def test_explicit_native_sizing_preserves_every_semantic_field_and_needs_approval(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared_chain(tmp_path)
    graph = measured_graph()
    provider = NativeFramingMock(graph)
    before = copy.deepcopy(graph)
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider)
    assert graph == before
    assert len(provider.requests) == 1
    assert plan["status"] == "proposed"
    assert store.get_quest(quest.id)["status"] != "approved"
    assert plan["edges"] == graph["edges"]
    for node, expected in zip(plan["nodes"], graph["nodes"], strict=True):
        expected = {
            **expected,
            "required_capabilities": {
                item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in expected["required_capabilities"]
            },
        }
        actual = {key: node[key] for key in expected if key != "budget_tokens"}
        assert actual == {key: value for key, value in expected.items() if key != "budget_tokens"}
        assert (
            node["budget_tokens"]
            == plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"][node["key"]]["initial_work_tokens"]
        )
    shared = plan["serial_capacity_policy"]["shared_reserve_tokens"]
    assert shared == max(
        item["minimum_node_tokens"] - item["initial_work_tokens"]
        for item in plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"].values()
    )
    assert (
        sum(node["budget_tokens"] for node in plan["nodes"])
        + shared
        + plan["coordination_reserve_tokens"]
        <= graph["max_total_tokens"]
    )
    provenance = plan["capacity_contract"]["resource_allocation"]
    assert provenance["fixed_point_verified"] is True
    assert 2 <= provenance["iterations"] <= 8
    assert all(
        item["initial_worker_request_measurement"]["native_input_reservation"] > 0
        for item in plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"].values()
    )
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM worker_runs").fetchone()[0] == 0
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mutation", ["total", "raw_packet", "context", "branch", "legacy"])
def test_impossible_measured_semantics_are_rejected_without_changing_bounds(tmp_path, mutation):
    store, quest = prepared_chain(tmp_path)
    graph = measured_graph()
    if mutation == "total":

def validate_serial_policy(graph):
    policy = graph.get("serial_capacity_policy")

    if (

## Explicit Core resource quantification

The capacity Planner wire offers `allocation_mode="core_measured_serial"` as
an explicit alternative to its legacy `model_declared` allocation. The model
still supplies the complete semantic DAG, role objectives, tools, success
criteria, input paths, predecessor handoffs and source/artifact/delivery byte
bounds. Core does not change those fields, the coordination reserve or the
original task ceiling. This mode supports only the same strict token-only
success chain. Model-supplied node budgets and serial-pool numbers are resource
placeholders rather than approved contracts.

Core measures every node with the production native request serializers and
the same complete source/review/correction policy. Initial baselines cover the
measured initial work; one shared pool covers the largest complete contingency.
Only resource numbers are iterated, for at most eight deterministic passes. A
pass must remeasure precisely the same resource vector before it is accepted;
non-convergence, packet/context overflow or original-cap overflow rejects the
proposal through the existing single repair opportunity. No extra model or tool
calls, receipts, budget reservations or allocation refunds occur in sizing.
The final ordinary preflight is mandatory. Its concrete baseline/pool numbers
and sizing provenance enter the digested proposal for normal plan/team approval.

For a remaining DAG, Core preserves the original pool and every completed node
baseline exactly. An unfinished baseline is the maximum of its measured initial
work and its complete cycle minus that unchanged pool. The original accounting
and residual-budget checks remain active. A parent without an approved serial
policy cannot silently become a serial revision through this mode. Ordinary
manual and legacy model-declared proposal behavior remains unchanged.

and `git diff --check` passed. The observation explicitly does not establish

## Three strict live failures

section is published. The following is a read-only observation, not a final
acceptance verdict.

| Level / run | Observed failure | Charged input / output | Settled attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L1 `20261115T092655Z-L1-c3a404` | Planner rejected before model dispatch | 3,661 / 572 | 2 |
| L2 `20261115T092655Z-L2-350db9` | Planner rejected before model dispatch | 3,747 / 619 | 2 |

`router` attempt, both settled with known input/output charges. There is no

turn them into real-model task acceptance. The semantic cross-Quest fixed sample
also retains its original failed oracle result; its separate independent audit
only supports the narrower source/trust-preserving retrieval observation.

V17 must remain an incomplete historical acceptance record if these outcomes are
confirmed. Subsequent fixes, tests and real runs require their own source manifest
and versioned evidence; they do not rewrite V17 outcomes.

# V16 full-suite failures: v17 compatibility proposal

The retained complete run is 1,304 passed / five failed / one existing warning in
328.69 seconds. All five failures are in the original M4 Planner tests; their
original schema, authorization, restart, no-Worker and lease-fencing assertions
must remain intact.

`test-compatibility-v17.patch` is a proposed change only. It has not been applied
and no proposed fixture has been run against the frozen source. Source and backend
tests remain unchanged pending integration-owner thaw.

Four failures arise because authenticated/background planning now explicitly uses
the capacity-aware contract, while the original fixtures return the old wire
shape with budgets of 10 or 100 tokens, no required-input/bounds/coordination
fields and no registered capacity-capable model. These cannot satisfy a real
Worker plus complete independent review/correction cycle. The race fixtures also
inherit the production model ledger default zero, which correctly leaves no
residual capacity. Replacing the service or mocking out preflight would bypass the
integration path under test.

The proposed patch adds one explicit Mock fixture helper and uses it only in:

- `test_expired_planner_attempt_cannot_modify_new_attempt` (both old-success and
  old-failure parameter cases);
- `test_authenticated_graph_controls_survive_restart_without_running_worker`;
- `test_user_turn_automatically_plans_once_without_extra_user_message`.

It registers a clearly labeled Mock profile with 65,536 context and 4,096 output,
sets an explicit 180,000-token local fixture budget, and returns one node with
150,000 cumulative allowance plus an 18,000 coordination reserve within the
180,000 total. It declares no input paths/tools/artifact and finite 2,048 source,
3,072 artifact and 1,536 delivery byte bounds. All values are test fixture
contracts, not measured production usage. The service's real schema validation,
capacity preflight, model eligibility and residual ledger checks still run.

Static AST comparison of the proposed complete test-file changes confirms all
original assertions are identical: 13 in `test_m4_adversarial.py`, 76 in
`test_m4_integration.py`. This does not prove the patch passes; after thaw it must
run the five original failures, both whole M4 modules and the capacity tests.

The fifth failure is different: `test_graph_planner_sends_strict_wire_schema_through_gateway`
correctly requires every object property to appear in `required`, with
`additionalProperties=false`. V16 added optional-default capacity properties to
legacy GraphWire/NodeWire, so their generated strict JSON schema violates that
Provider contract before response parsing. Its assertion must remain unchanged.
The Graph/schema owner is handling the source correction separately. Prefer a
legacy wire class with the original required fields plus an explicit capacity
wire subclass requiring the new fields, preserving local manual-plan defaults.
Do not fix this by weakening the test, removing `strict`, or silently ignoring
new fields at the Provider boundary.

This proposal changes no original run record and does not certify a live Planner
fix. Real strict live failures are separately diagnosed on their exact source.

# FORGE 项目状态

更新：2026-11-15。分支：`codex/phase1-continuous`。

**V17 正在验收：最终冻结源码、完整后端套件和 strict L1/L2/L3 的结果待集成负责人填入。本草稿不宣布 Phase 2 完成。** 当前任务集中于 Agent Intelligence；桌面前端由另一个窗口维护，安装包与发布不属于本轮交付。

FORGE 保留一个长期 `main` 对话，Router 是唯一面向用户的 Agent。后端已经连接模型驱动 Router、独立 Planner、审批后的 DAG/团队、后台 Worker、受治理工具、独立上下文审阅、返工、上下文归档和原文回读。记忆包含来源约束、词法检索以及有预算的模型语义选择。计划、团队、危险工具及证据门槛继续由 Core 执行。

V17 补齐了自动反馈重规划入口：Router 可针对停止的部分完成 DAG 生成 `quest.replan_requested`，后台 Planner 再提出保留完成证据的 remaining DAG。新计划和团队仍须明确批准，事件本身不授权执行。受约束的层次展开要求新的计划/团队审批，不能增加父节点原预算、工具或深度。

V17 的直接前驱交付工具重验批准的成功前驱、原始结果事件、八字段完整交付及原证据。交付仍是未验证模型声明，后继必须执行自己的任务并通过自己的审查。归档原文、前驱回执和完整交付读取由验收器按各自来源证据验证，不伪造文件动作回执，也不满足最终文件要求。

新增 `serial-capacity-v1` 是明确批准的串行共享应急额度，仅支持成功单链、并发一和无费用上限的 Token 预算。每个后续节点的初始工作基础额度受到保留；共享池只登记一次。实际请求仍由原 Gateway 账本约束，已花费、未结算和未知调用不会退款。应急池耗尽会阻断任务，不能保证所有节点最坏情况下的审阅、修复都成功。

本地专项证据包括：[Core 请求与验收兼容 88 项](audit/phase2/core-framing-driver-v17-regression.xml)、[串行/前驱 48 项联合回归](audit/phase2/serial-native-regression-v17.xml)、[串行 Runtime 最终 3 项](audit/phase2/serial-runtime-v17-final.xml)。这些集合有重叠，不能相加为完整套件。原生 Gateway 的本地脚本 HTTP fixture 使用实际账本、工具、审阅和重开 Store；其技术 `execution_mode=live` 不表示实际模型或真实任务成功。

历史 V16 全套保留 1,304 passed、5 failed、1 个已有 warning / 328.69 秒，三层 strict live 均失败于 Planner 提案阶段。V16 固定算法研究的 90 行全部完成模型阶段，但任务成功仅 25/90；65 个失败保留，135 次真实模型调用，输入/输出 91,487/19,756 Token。不能把完成调用或正确账本当成任务成功。

V17 单次跨任务语义记忆探针使用真实模型和原 Gateway，1 次调用、1,713/113 输入/输出 Token、未知 0。模型选择了正确来源的决定和约束；原探针因候选枚举漏掉自动生成的同来源约束而记为失败，原结果保留。独立补充审计可说明实际来源/信任保持，不能追认原探针全项通过、重抽样本或证明复杂 Quest 完成。

当前仍需分别验证：复杂目标的实际产物正确性、失败/返工/压缩/重启后的完整连续性、多个模型选择的效果，以及真实多 Quest 并行完成。图像/音频/视频输入执行不可用；明确转入 `needs_input` 只说明诚实处理能力限制。任意 shell、无限制 Python、一般仓库补丁/测试执行不属于现有受治理工具范围。未配置可信价格时费用保持未知。

最终证据入口为 [Phase 2 状态](PHASE2_STATUS.md)、[报告](PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md)、[实验](PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md)、[质量门槛](QUALITY_GATES.md)及 `docs/audit/phase2/verification.json`。集成负责人应在保留旧文档完整副本后发布本版，并用实际冻结哈希、全套计数和 run ID 替换验收待定状态。Phase 1 Milestone 1–7 报告及全部失败实验继续保留。

本轮完成门槛是同一冻结源码上的全量回归、静态检查、依赖检查、保留性审计及当前 strict L1/L2/L3。复杂场景必须有实际产物、独立检查以及中途 Core 重启后的连续执行；预期的失败、返工、压缩、原文回读也必须在实际记录中观察到。缺失观察不能写成通过。

# FORGE 质量门槛

更新：2026-11-15。V17 最终冻结与验收待定。本文件描述应满足的标准，不能用待运行项目替代结果。

1. 所有后端源代码、实验驱动和测试在同一 manifest 下冻结，跑完整后端套件以及 Ruff、格式、依赖和 diff 检查。局部集合有重叠，不能累加。源码变化后旧结果只证明旧快照。
2. Phase 1 报告、旧测试身份、原始失败数据库、日志与实验结果完整保留。兼容 fixture 修改必须披露；不得删除断言、伪造运行数据、隐藏失败或覆盖原 run。
3. 实际模型实验走原 Gateway、有限持久预算、原能力/输出/context/重试/并发边界。逐 HTTP attempt 计入 settled 用量或完整未知预留；费用未知保持 null，不能当作零。
4. 区分实际模型、本地脚本 HTTP、Mock、合成实验。Gateway 连接本地脚本服务时自然产生的 `execution_mode=live` 只证明原生传输和账本路径，不能成为真实模型质量或 strict 任务验收证据。
5. 当前 strict L1/L2/L3 必须由只读验收器根据原数据库和实际文件重新验证。成功的 HTTP、合法提案、通过的测试、模型自报或过往版本成功均不能替代当前任务成功。
6. L1 保持单 Worker、真实只读文件读取/目录回执、完整八字段交付与当前独立 PASS；L2/L3 保持专业角色、完整最终产物、真实哈希/回执/固定检查和当前内容审查。复杂任务还须实际中途重启、身份/计数/来源保留以及成功恢复完成。
7. 原始目标和更新目标、来源约束、批准图/团队及当前结果必须绑定。来源撤销、修改、过期、跨任务错配、过时 PASS、权限扩展或未知效果均不能继续授权。
8. `worker_read_context_source`、`worker_read_action_receipt`、`worker_read_completed_delivery` 按 Core 原来源及绑定的 Worker exchange 重验。其结果不伪造成 action receipt，不满足独立的源文件读取、文件创建或最终产物要求。前驱交付必须完整、保留原字节上限并重验完整成功证据；其内容仍为模型声明。
9. 新容量合同测量实际来源、原生 Gateway 序列化、输出以及有界审阅/纠错。`serial-capacity-v1` 必须由用户明确批准，限定成功单链/并发一/Token-only；基础额度及一次共享池之和在原任务 cap 内。未来节点基础额度受到保护。所有未结算、拒绝、超额及未知 attempt 按原账本保守处理，不因启动、重启或重新组队退款。

V17 最终全量、strict run ID、manifest 哈希及独立保留性审计由集成负责人根据真实产物填写。历史结果保留在 `docs/audit/phase2/`；未观察或失败检查不能在最终文档中改成通过。

1. 所有后端源代码、实验驱动和测试在同一 manifest 下冻结，跑完整后端套件以及 Ruff、格式、依赖和 diff 检查。局部集合有重叠，不能累加。源码变化后旧结果只证明旧快照。
2. Phase 1 报告、旧测试身份、原始失败数据库、日志与实验结果完整保留。兼容 fixture 修改必须披露；不得删除断言、伪造运行数据、隐藏失败或覆盖原 run。
3. 实际模型实验走原 Gateway、有限持久预算、原能力/输出/context/重试/并发边界。逐 HTTP attempt 计入 settled 用量或完整未知预留；费用未知保持 null，不能当作零。
4. 区分实际模型、本地脚本 HTTP、Mock、合成实验。Gateway 连接本地脚本服务时自然产生的 `execution_mode=live` 只证明原生传输和账本路径，不能成为真实模型质量或 strict 任务验收证据。
5. 当前 strict L1/L2/L3 必须由只读验收器根据原数据库和实际文件重新验证。成功的 HTTP、合法提案、通过的测试、模型自报或过往版本成功均不能替代当前任务成功。
6. L1 保持单 Worker、真实只读文件读取/目录回执、完整八字段交付与当前独立 PASS；L2/L3 保持专业角色、完整最终产物、真实哈希/回执/固定检查和当前内容审查。复杂任务还须实际中途重启、身份/计数/来源保留以及成功恢复完成。
7. 原始目标和更新目标、来源约束、批准图/团队及当前结果必须绑定。来源撤销、修改、过期、跨任务错配、过时 PASS、权限扩展或未知效果均不能继续授权。
8. `worker_read_context_source`、`worker_read_action_receipt`、`worker_read_completed_delivery` 按 Core 原来源及绑定的 Worker exchange 重验。其结果不伪造成 action receipt，不满足独立的源文件读取、文件创建或最终产物要求。前驱交付必须完整、保留原字节上限并重验完整成功证据；其内容仍为模型声明。
9. 新容量合同测量实际来源、原生 Gateway 序列化、输出以及有界审阅/纠错。`serial-capacity-v1` 必须由用户明确批准，限定成功单链/并发一/Token-only；基础额度及一次共享池之和在原任务 cap 内。未来节点基础额度受到保护。所有未结算、拒绝、超额及未知 attempt 按原账本保守处理，不因启动、重启或重新组队退款。
10. Worker 修复、审阅返工、Agent 派生、步骤、工具和时间均有界。租约更替、暂停/撤销或过时响应不能恢复旧执行权；准确结算历史已知 usage 只修账，不授予响应应用或重放权。
11. Benchmark 固定任务、预算、基线、评分规则和全部原始结果。必须同时报告任务成功、Token/调用、耗时、返工和证据完整性。模型阶段完成率与任务成功率分开；单模型、小样本、不同调用次数和反馈差异必须披露。

能力边界：语义记忆是有限候选页的模型选择，保留原身份、哈希和信任，无法证明大规模/跨领域检索质量。反馈重规划只生成新提案，不能自动批准。受限层次展开不等于无限 Agent。图像/音频/视频执行、任意 shell 与通用仓库编辑/测试执行未实现。同模型新上下文审阅不具备模型多样性，证据门槛也不证明任意领域正确性。

V17 最终全量、strict run ID、manifest 哈希及独立保留性审计由集成负责人根据真实产物填写。历史结果保留在 `docs/audit/phase2/`；未观察或失败检查不能在最终文档中改成通过。

"""Recorded Router decisions replayed offline through the actual creation path."""

import asyncio
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from test_router_intelligence_phase2 import ScriptedMock, router

from forge_core.domain import DomainError, ModelProfile, Quest
from forge_core.providers import ProviderConfig, ProviderGateway
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
from forge_core.settings import Workspace
from forge_core.store import Store


class Captured(Exception):
    pass


class NativeCapture(ProviderGateway):
    """Production framing and no network/model request."""

    def __init__(self, *, repair=False):
        super().__init__(
            ProviderConfig(
                id="p",
                kind="openai_compatible",
                base_url="https://example.invalid/v1",
                credential_ref="FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_TEST",
                supports_json_schema=True,
            )
        )
        self.requests = []
        self.native_sizes = []
        self.repair = repair

    async def generate(self, request):
        native = self._payload(request, False)
        self.requests.append(request)
        self.native_sizes.append(
            len(json.dumps(native, ensure_ascii=False).encode()) + 64
        )
        if self.repair and len(self.requests) == 1:
            return type("InvalidResponse", (), {"text": "{}", "usage": {}})()
        raise Captured


def route_original_scenario(tmp_path, level):
    root = next(parent / "backend" for parent in Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (parent / "backend/scripts/phase2/acceptance_scenarios.py").is_file())
    module_path = root / "scripts/phase2/acceptance_scenarios.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("planner_v18_scenario", module_path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    prompt = module.seed_scenario(level, tmp_path)["prompt"]
    fixture = json.loads(
        (Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures/phase2_router_decisions_v17.json").read_text(
            encoding="utf-8"
        )
    )
    observed = fixture["cases"][level - 1]["decision"]
    store = Store(tmp_path / "core.sqlite3", workspace=Workspace.from_path(tmp_path))
    store.save_model(ModelProfile.model_validate(fixture["model_profile"]))
    result = asyncio.run(
        router(store, ScriptedMock(observed)).handle_user_message(
            prompt, request_id=f"scenario-{level}"
        )
    )
    return store, store.get_quest(result["quest_id"]), prompt, observed


@pytest.mark.parametrize("level", [1, 2, 3])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("repair", [False, True])
def test_actual_router_quest_shape_retains_full_sources_and_fits_native_planner(
    tmp_path, level, repair
):
    store, quest, original, observed = route_original_scenario(tmp_path, level)
    provider = NativeCapture(repair=repair)
    with pytest.raises(Captured):
        asyncio.run(
            QuestGraphService(store).generate(
                quest["id"],
                expected_version=quest["version"],
                provider=provider,
                provider_id="p",
                model_id="native",
                context_limit=65536,
                capabilities={"json_schema": True},
                capability_sources={"json_schema": "test_fixture"},
                require_capacity_contract=True,
            )
        )
    assert len(provider.requests) == (2 if repair else 1)
    data = json.loads(provider.requests[0].messages[1]["content"])
    assert data["original_request"]["content"] == original
    assert data["goal"] == observed["goal"]
    assert data["user_constraints"]["items"]
    assert data["verified_input_inventory"]
    assert (
        data["execution_constraints"]["limits"]["max_total_tokens"]
        == {1: 180000, 2: 360000, 3: 630000}[level]
    )
    for request, native in zip(provider.requests, provider.native_sizes, strict=True):
        assert request.context_limit == 65536
        assert native + request.max_output_tokens <= request.context_limit
        assert (
            request.messages[1]["content"]
            == provider.requests[0].messages[1]["content"]
        )
    assert QuestGraphService(store).history(quest["id"]) == []


def test_native_planner_context_rejects_full_policy_and_schema_before_provider(
    tmp_path,
):
    store, quest, _original, _observed = route_original_scenario(tmp_path, 3)
    provider = NativeCapture()
    with pytest.raises(DomainError, match="Planner context budget exceeded"):
        asyncio.run(
            QuestGraphService(store).generate(
                quest["id"],
                expected_version=quest["version"],
                provider=provider,
                provider_id="p",
                model_id="native",
                context_limit=28000,
                capabilities={"json_schema": True},
                capability_sources={"json_schema": "test_fixture"},
                require_capacity_contract=True,
            )
        )
    assert provider.requests == []


def test_planner_content_bound_remains_finite_without_truncating_goal(tmp_path):
    store = Store(tmp_path / "core.sqlite3", workspace=Workspace.from_path(tmp_path))
    quest = Quest(title="Oversize", goal="完整约束" * 10000)
    store.save_quest(quest)
    provider = NativeCapture()
    with pytest.raises(DomainError, match="Quest is too large to plan"):
        asyncio.run(
            QuestGraphService(store).generate(
                quest.id,
                expected_version=0,
                provider=provider,
                provider_id="p",
                model_id="native",
                context_limit=65536,
                capabilities={"json_schema": True},
                capability_sources={"json_schema": "test_fixture"},
                require_capacity_contract=True,
            )
        )
    assert provider.requests == []
    assert store.get_quest(quest.id)["goal"] == quest.goal

    def proposal_data(self, *, completed_nodes=()):
        data = self.model_dump()

            if len({item["name"] for item in capabilities}) != len(capabilities):
                raise ValueError("Duplicate capability")
            node["required_capabilities"] = {item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in capabilities}
        data["nodes"].extend(completed_nodes)

    def proposal(self, *, completed_nodes=()):
        data = self.proposal_data(completed_nodes=completed_nodes)

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: D:/Competition_this/Agent/.local/phase2/planner-semantic-diagnostics-v19/planner_diagnostics.py
+"""Bounded observations for one Planner repair; never decide graph validity.
+
+Only node keys, artifact/input paths and edge keys are inspected. Objectives,
+source text, model responses and other graph fields are never copied. The normal
+schema/capacity validators remain authoritative; this helper never changes data,
+executes tools, calls a Provider or repairs a graph.
+"""
+
+import json
+import re
+
+VERSION = "planner-semantic-diagnostics-v1"
+MAX_NODES = 8
+MAX_EDGES = 16
+MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE = 32
+MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS = 32
+MAX_INVALID_PATHS = 16
+MAX_PATH_CHARS = 240
+MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS = 2000
+MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES = 8192
+_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}\Z")
+
+
+def semantic_graph_diagnostics(data, verified_paths=()):
+    """Describe unavailable inputs and one cycle within strict output bounds.
+
+    ``data`` is a semantic wire dictionary, before GraphProposal validation;
+    ``verified_paths`` contains only already verified inventory path strings.
+    Path visibility follows the existing capacity preflight: verified inputs or
+    one direct success/always predecessor artifact. A missing success edge is
+    supplemental detail, not a new rule excluding a valid ``always`` edge.
+    An empty report never proves validity. Truncation is explicitly recorded.
+    """
+    report = {
+        "version": VERSION,
+        "invalid_input_paths": [],
+        "cycle_witness": [],
+        "truncated": False,
+        "omitted": {"nodes": 0, "edges": 0, "input_paths": 0, "input_diagnostics": 0},
+    }
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        report["truncated"] = True
+        return report
+
+    def label(value):
+        if not isinstance(value, str):
+            return "<non-string>"
+        if len(value) > MAX_PATH_CHARS:
+            report["truncated"] = True
+            return value[: MAX_PATH_CHARS - 1] + "…"
+        return value
+
+    raw_nodes = data.get("nodes")
+    raw_edges = data.get("edges")
+    if not isinstance(raw_nodes, list) or not isinstance(raw_edges, list):
+        report["truncated"] = True
+        return report
+    report["omitted"]["nodes"] = max(0, len(raw_nodes) - MAX_NODES)
+    report["omitted"]["edges"] = max(0, len(raw_edges) - MAX_EDGES)
+    report["truncated"] = bool(report["omitted"]["nodes"] or report["omitted"]["edges"])
+    nodes = []
+    for node in raw_nodes[:MAX_NODES]:
+        if not isinstance(node, dict) or not isinstance(node.get("key"), str):
+            report["truncated"] = True
+            continue
+        key = node["key"]
+        if len(key) > 100 or _KEY.fullmatch(key) is None:
+            report["truncated"] = True
+            continue
+        nodes.append(node)
+    keys = {node["key"] for node in nodes}
+
+    edges = []
+    for edge in raw_edges[:MAX_EDGES]:
+        if not isinstance(edge, dict):
+            report["truncated"] = True
+            continue
+        source, target, condition = (edge.get(key) for key in ("source", "target", "condition"))
+        if (
+            not isinstance(source, str)
+            or not isinstance(target, str)
+            or source not in keys
+            or target not in keys
+            or condition not in ("success", "failure", "always")
+        ):
+            report["truncated"] = True
+            continue
+        edges.append({"source": source, "target": target, "condition": condition})
+
+    verified = set()
+    if isinstance(verified_paths, (list, tuple)):
+        if len(verified_paths) > MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS:
+            report["truncated"] = True
+        for path in verified_paths[:MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS]:
+            if isinstance(path, str) and len(path) <= MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS:
+                verified.add(path)
+            else:
+                report["truncated"] = True
+    else:
+        report["truncated"] = True
+
+    invalid_count = 0
+    for node in nodes:
+        paths = node.get("required_input_paths")
+        if paths is None:

Only node keys, artifact/input paths and edge keys are inspected. Objectives,
source text, model responses and other graph fields are never copied. The normal
schema/capacity validators remain authoritative; this helper never changes data,
executes tools, calls a Provider or repairs a graph.

import json
import re

VERSION = "planner-semantic-diagnostics-v1"
MAX_NODES = 8
MAX_EDGES = 16
MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE = 32
MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS = 32
MAX_INVALID_PATHS = 16
MAX_PATH_CHARS = 240
MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS = 2000
MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES = 8192
_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}\Z")


def semantic_graph_diagnostics(data, verified_paths=()):
    """Describe unavailable inputs and one cycle within strict output bounds.

    ``data`` is a semantic wire dictionary, before GraphProposal validation;
    ``verified_paths`` contains only already verified inventory path strings.
    Path visibility follows the existing capacity preflight: verified inputs or
    one direct success/always predecessor artifact. A missing success edge is
    supplemental detail, not a new rule excluding a valid ``always`` edge.
    An empty report never proves validity. Truncation is explicitly recorded.
    """
    report = {
        "version": VERSION,
        "invalid_input_paths": [],
        "cycle_witness": [],
        "truncated": False,
        "omitted": {"nodes": 0, "edges": 0, "input_paths": 0, "input_diagnostics": 0},
    }
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        report["truncated"] = True
        return report

    def label(value):
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            return "<non-string>"
        if len(value) > MAX_PATH_CHARS:
            report["truncated"] = True
            return value[: MAX_PATH_CHARS - 1] + "…"
        return value

    raw_nodes = data.get("nodes")
    raw_edges = data.get("edges")
    if not isinstance(raw_nodes, list) or not isinstance(raw_edges, list):
        report["truncated"] = True
        return report
    report["omitted"]["nodes"] = max(0, len(raw_nodes) - MAX_NODES)
    report["omitted"]["edges"] = max(0, len(raw_edges) - MAX_EDGES)
    report["truncated"] = bool(report["omitted"]["nodes"] or report["omitted"]["edges"])
    nodes = []
    for node in raw_nodes[:MAX_NODES]:
        if not isinstance(node, dict) or not isinstance(node.get("key"), str):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        key = node["key"]
        if len(key) > 100 or _KEY.fullmatch(key) is None:
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        nodes.append(node)
    keys = {node["key"] for node in nodes}

    edges = []
    for edge in raw_edges[:MAX_EDGES]:
        if not isinstance(edge, dict):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        source, target, condition = (edge.get(key) for key in ("source", "target", "condition"))
        if (
            not isinstance(source, str)
            or not isinstance(target, str)
            or source not in keys
            or target not in keys
            or condition not in ("success", "failure", "always")
        ):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        edges.append({"source": source, "target": target, "condition": condition})

    verified = set()
    if isinstance(verified_paths, (list, tuple)):
        if len(verified_paths) > MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS:
            report["truncated"] = True
        for path in verified_paths[:MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS]:
            if isinstance(path, str) and len(path) <= MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS:
                verified.add(path)
            else:
                report["truncated"] = True
    else:
        report["truncated"] = True

    invalid_count = 0
    for node in nodes:
        paths = node.get("required_input_paths")
        if paths is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(paths, list):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        report["omitted"]["input_paths"] += max(0, len(paths) - MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE)
        for path in paths[:MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE]:
            valid_identity = isinstance(path, str) and len(path) <= MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS
            if valid_identity and path in verified:
                continue
            producers = [
                other["key"]
                for other in nodes
                if valid_identity and other.get("expected_artifact") == path
            ]
            visible = [
                edge["source"]
                for edge in edges
                if edge["target"] == node["key"]
                and edge["source"] in producers
                and edge["condition"] in ("success", "always")
            ]
            if len(producers) == 1 and visible:
                continue
            invalid_count += 1
            if len(report["invalid_input_paths"]) >= MAX_INVALID_PATHS:
                continue
            report["invalid_input_paths"].append(
                {
                    "node": node["key"],
                    "path": label(path),
                    "self_output": valid_identity and node.get("expected_artifact") == path,
                    "actual_producers": producers,
                    "missing_direct_success_edge": bool(producers)
                    and not any(
                        edge["source"] in producers
                        and edge["target"] == node["key"]
                        and edge["condition"] == "success"
                        for edge in edges
                    ),
                }
            )

    # GraphProposal checks cycles across every edge condition. The witness keeps
    # the exact observed edge keys/conditions; it does not invent a repair.
    adjacency = {key: [] for key in keys}
    for edge in edges:
        adjacency[edge["source"]].append(edge)
    states = {}
    stack_nodes, stack_edges = [], []

    def visit(key):
        states[key] = 1
        stack_nodes.append(key)
        for edge in adjacency[key]:
            target = edge["target"]
            if states.get(target) == 1:
                start = stack_nodes.index(target)
                return stack_edges[start:] + [edge]
            if states.get(target, 0) == 0:
                stack_edges.append(edge)
                witness = visit(target)
                if witness:
                    return witness
                stack_edges.pop()
        stack_nodes.pop()
        states[key] = 2
        return []

    for node in nodes:
        if states.get(node["key"], 0) == 0:
            witness = visit(node["key"])
            if witness:
                report["cycle_witness"] = [dict(edge) for edge in witness]
                break

    report["omitted"]["input_diagnostics"] = invalid_count - len(report["invalid_input_paths"])
    report["truncated"] = report["truncated"] or any(report["omitted"].values())
    while len(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")) > MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES:
        # A cycle has at most eight ASCII-keyed edges, so removing path rows is
        # always sufficient. Preserve the witness while bounding repair input.
        report["invalid_input_paths"].pop()
        report["omitted"]["input_diagnostics"] += 1
        report["truncated"] = True
    return report

"""Bounded observations for one Planner repair; never decide graph validity.

Only node keys, artifact/input paths and edge keys are inspected. Objectives,
source text, model responses and other graph fields are never copied. The normal
schema/capacity validators remain authoritative; this helper never changes data,
executes tools, calls a Provider or repairs a graph.
"""

import json
import re

VERSION = "planner-semantic-diagnostics-v1"
MAX_NODES = 8
MAX_EDGES = 16
MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE = 32
MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS = 32
MAX_INVALID_PATHS = 16
MAX_PATH_CHARS = 240
MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS = 2000
MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES = 8192
_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}\Z")


def semantic_graph_diagnostics(data, verified_paths=()):
    """Describe unavailable inputs and one cycle within strict output bounds.

    ``data`` is a semantic wire dictionary, before GraphProposal validation;
    ``verified_paths`` contains only already verified inventory path strings.
    Path visibility follows the existing capacity preflight: verified inputs or
    one direct success/always predecessor artifact. A missing success edge is
    supplemental detail, not a new rule excluding a valid ``always`` edge.
    An empty report never proves validity. Truncation is explicitly recorded.
    """
    report = {
        "version": VERSION,
        "invalid_input_paths": [],
        "cycle_witness": [],
        "truncated": False,
        "omitted": {"nodes": 0, "edges": 0, "input_paths": 0, "input_diagnostics": 0},
    }
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        report["truncated"] = True
        return report

    def label(value):
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            return "<non-string>"
        if len(value) > MAX_PATH_CHARS:
            report["truncated"] = True
            return value[: MAX_PATH_CHARS - 1] + "…"
        return value

    raw_nodes = data.get("nodes")
    raw_edges = data.get("edges")
    if not isinstance(raw_nodes, list) or not isinstance(raw_edges, list):
        report["truncated"] = True
        return report
    report["omitted"]["nodes"] = max(0, len(raw_nodes) - MAX_NODES)
    report["omitted"]["edges"] = max(0, len(raw_edges) - MAX_EDGES)
    report["truncated"] = bool(report["omitted"]["nodes"] or report["omitted"]["edges"])
    nodes = []
    for node in raw_nodes[:MAX_NODES]:
        if not isinstance(node, dict) or not isinstance(node.get("key"), str):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        key = node["key"]
        if len(key) > 100 or _KEY.fullmatch(key) is None:
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        nodes.append(node)
    keys = {node["key"] for node in nodes}

    edges = []
    for edge in raw_edges[:MAX_EDGES]:
        if not isinstance(edge, dict):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        source, target, condition = (edge.get(key) for key in ("source", "target", "condition"))
        if (
            not isinstance(source, str)
            or not isinstance(target, str)
            or source not in keys
            or target not in keys
            or condition not in ("success", "failure", "always")
        ):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        edges.append({"source": source, "target": target, "condition": condition})

    verified = set()
    if isinstance(verified_paths, (list, tuple)):
        if len(verified_paths) > MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS:
            report["truncated"] = True
        for path in verified_paths[:MAX_VERIFIED_PATHS]:
            if isinstance(path, str) and len(path) <= MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS:
                verified.add(path)
            else:
                report["truncated"] = True
    else:
        report["truncated"] = True

    invalid_count = 0
    for node in nodes:
        paths = node.get("required_input_paths")
        if paths is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(paths, list):
            report["truncated"] = True
            continue
        report["omitted"]["input_paths"] += max(0, len(paths) - MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE)
        for path in paths[:MAX_PATHS_PER_NODE]:
            valid_identity = isinstance(path, str) and len(path) <= MAX_IDENTITY_CHARS
            if valid_identity and path in verified:
                continue
            producers = [
                other["key"]
                for other in nodes
                if valid_identity and other.get("expected_artifact") == path
            ]
            visible = [
                edge["source"]
                for edge in edges
                if edge["target"] == node["key"]
                and edge["source"] in producers
                and edge["condition"] in ("success", "always")
            ]
            if len(producers) == 1 and visible:
                continue
            invalid_count += 1
            if len(report["invalid_input_paths"]) >= MAX_INVALID_PATHS:
                continue
            report["invalid_input_paths"].append(
                {
                    "node": node["key"],
                    "path": label(path),
                    "self_output": valid_identity and node.get("expected_artifact") == path,
                    "actual_producers": producers,
                    "missing_direct_success_edge": not any(
                        edge["source"] in producers
                        and edge["target"] == node["key"]
                        and edge["condition"] == "success"
                        for edge in edges
                    ),
                }
            )

    # GraphProposal checks cycles across every edge condition. The witness keeps
    # the exact observed edge keys/conditions; it does not invent a repair.
    adjacency = {key: [] for key in keys}
    for edge in edges:
        adjacency[edge["source"]].append(edge)
    states = {}
    stack_nodes, stack_edges = [], []

    def visit(key):
        states[key] = 1
        stack_nodes.append(key)
        for edge in adjacency[key]:
            target = edge["target"]
            if states.get(target) == 1:
                start = stack_nodes.index(target)
                return stack_edges[start:] + [edge]
            if states.get(target, 0) == 0:
                stack_edges.append(edge)
                witness = visit(target)
                if witness:
                    return witness
                stack_edges.pop()
        stack_nodes.pop()
        states[key] = 2
        return []

    for node in nodes:
        if states.get(node["key"], 0) == 0:
            witness = visit(node["key"])
            if witness:
                report["cycle_witness"] = [dict(edge) for edge in witness]
                break

    report["omitted"]["input_diagnostics"] = invalid_count - len(report["invalid_input_paths"])
    report["truncated"] = report["truncated"] or any(report["omitted"].values())
    while len(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")) > MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES:
        # A cycle has at most eight ASCII-keyed edges, so removing path rows is
        # always sufficient. Preserve the witness while bounding repair input.
        report["invalid_input_paths"].pop()
        report["omitted"]["input_diagnostics"] += 1
        report["truncated"] = True
    return report
